newsitem.title: USA: United Acquisition II files Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: United Acquisition II files Chapter 11.

text.p: United Acquisition II Corp said on Tuesday that it filed Chapter 11 at the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in the Southern District of New York.
The reasons for the filing made on February 28, 1997, centered on a $2 million lawsuit filed by Fidelity Business Alliance, United Acquisition said.
Also, United Acquisition cited a claim by former shareholders of Mid-America Transporters Group Inc, the company's principal asset, as a reason for the filing.
United Acquisition said it plans to proceed with claims against Mid-America's former shareholders, since they are attempting to sell Mid-America without legally owning it.

The company's series B preferred shareholders funded the retention of the company's bankruptcy counsel through the conversion of outstanding series B preferred shares were originally issued for an aggregate purchase price of $154,500, the company said.
Upon conversion of the series B preferred shares into common stock, the preferred B shareholders paid an additional aggregate of $20,800, United Acquisition said.
United Acquisition was not immediately available for further comment.
